lines: On a misty night in Ireland, an old family hears a cry outside the window.
It is not the wind, and it is not a fox.
In Irish tales, it is the banshee, the woman of the fairy mound.
She is pale, with long grey hair and eyes red from weeping.
Some say she sits on a stone, combing her hair and wailing.
She only cries for certain old families, with names starting with O or Mac.
Her cry is a warning that death is near.
Old folk say never pick up a comb lying on the ground in the dark.
title: The Wailing Woman Who Warns Irish Families of Death #shorts
description:
In Irish folklore the banshee wails outside the homes of old families to warn that death is near. Never pick up a comb you find in the dark.
